adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed the fallback from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. But this expression is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (due to the ternary), so the predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, which will almost always return no match and yield `undefined`. This makes the fallback path effectively broken/dead: `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` becomes `undefined` when `externalCalendarId` isn’t provided. Unlike `createEvent` (which explicitly falls back to `"primary"`), the shown `updateEvent` code does not show a `|| "primary"` safeguard, so it can call `calendar.events.update` with an undefined `calendarId`. For `deleteEvent`, the new fallback similarly won’t select the intended destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` is missing, leading to wrong-calendar behavior.
